test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-2) Official Paper (Held On: 13 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the compound interest on Rs. 2,50,000 at 16% per annum for 9 months, compounded quarterly?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **quarterly compounding**, the **Rate** becomes 16% ÷ 4 = 4% and **Time** becomes 9 ÷ 3 = 3 periods.

Use the **3 : 3 : 1 ratio method** for 3 periods at 4%:

Step 1: 4% of 2,50,000 = 10,000 | Step 2: 4% of 10,000 = 400 | Step 3: 4% of 400 = 16

**Compound Interest** = 3 × (10,000) + 3 × (400) + 1 × (16) = 30,000 + 1,200 + 16 = 31,216.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 31,216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Principal (P)** = Rs. 2,50,000

⇒ **Annual Rate (R)** = 16%

⇒ **Time (T)** = 9 months

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Amount (A)** = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where r is the quarterly rate and n is the number of quarters.

⇒ **Compound Interest (CI)** = Amount − Principal

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b84660cb2ed51463fe84a9e71f98cb7bc2c3fab921ce2e62fad79d22ffd96694.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Quarterly Rate (r) = 16% ÷ 4 = 4%

⇒ Number of quarters (n) = 9 months ÷ 3 months = 3 quarters

⇒ A = 2,50,000 × (1 + 4/100)³

⇒ A = 2,50,000 × (1.04)³

⇒ A = 2,50,000 × 1.124864

⇒ A = 281,216

⇒ CI = 281,216 − 2,50,000

⇒ CI = 31,216

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 31,216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Quarterly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded quarterly, divide the annual rate by 4 and multiply the time in years by 4. Formula: A = P(1 + R/400)⁴ⁿ.

Half-Yearly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded half-yearly, divide the annual rate by 2 and multiply the time in years by 2. Formula: A = P(1 + R/200)²ⁿ.

Effective Interest Rate

It represents the actual interest earned in a year due to compounding. Effective Rate = (1 + r/n)ⁿ − 1, where r is the nominal rate and n is the frequency.

CI − SI Difference for 3 Years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for 3 years is given by: D = P(r/100)² × (3 + r/100).</p
